narrative.overview:
Solvance is a Bay Area tech-design agency at 11pm — screens glowing, builds shipping, no clients watching. The aesthetic is not austere minimalism or corporate polish; it's the confident messiness of a studio that ships world-class work and doesn't need to announce it. Dark surfaces, electric signals in blue and violet, typography that moves with precision.

The palette is a deep studio void cut through with blue signal light. Motion is orchestrated and purposeful: Awwwards-tier entrance choreography, Active Theory–level scroll presence. Every surface reacts to the cursor. Nothing sits inert. The site should leave a visitor asking 'how did they build that?' — the answer is Solvance, and that's the whole pitch.

This system explicitly rejects: hustle-culture excitement (no '10x your revenue,' no emoji-heavy energy), corporate formality (no IBM-weight, no formal grid layouts, no impersonal committee-designed sections), and the generic AI landing page (no hero-metric template, no cream/warm-neutral backgrounds, no floating feature icon cards, no eyebrow labels on every section heading).
keyCharacteristics: Near-void dark background (#0A0A0C) as the foundation — not dark gray, not navy, but the absence of light
Two signal colors (Bay Signal Blue + Studio Violet) used as emitters, not fills
Geist as the single type family: precise, geometric, the font of the builder generation
Cursor-tracked radial glows on every interactive surface
Spring physics on all hover interactions (Framer Motion)
Lenis smooth scroll — the scroll feel is part of the brand

rules.name: The Emitter Rule
rules.body: Bay Signal Blue and Studio Violet are light sources, not fills. They belong on small high-contrast elements (buttons, badges, glows, active indicators) and in gradients. A large blue surface is a violation — blue is rare here, and rarity is the point.

rules.name: The Temperature Rule
rules.body: Every neutral has a cool undertone. Warm grays, cream, or sand backgrounds are prohibited — they conflict with the cold-light signal palette and read as a different brand entirely.

rules.name: The Compression Rule
rules.body: Display and Headline headings use tight leading (0.96–1.02) and strong negative tracking (-0.03em to -0.04em). Loose leading on large type reads as unconfident. If a heading wraps, text-wrap: balance prevents orphans.

rules.name: The Mono-as-Mark Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono signals technical precision. It appears on category labels, code, and stat suffixes — not on body copy, nav links, or marketing headings. Its rarity is what makes it mean something.

rules.name: The Cursor-as-Light Rule
rules.body: Elevation is not static — it follows the user. Every card surface tracks cursor position via --glow-x / --glow-y CSS custom properties and emits a 380px radial blue glow. Static flat cards are prohibited.

rules.name: The Flat-at-Rest Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Deep shadows appear only as a response to hover. A resting card does not lift itself out of the page.

dos: Do keep the background at #0A0A0C (Studio Void). It is not dark gray and not navy.
Do use Bay Signal Blue sparingly as an emitter. CTAs, glows, active indicators, gradient accents only.
Do add cursor-tracked glow (--glow-x / --glow-y + SpringCard) to every interactive card surface.
Do use Geist Mono exclusively for labels, stat suffixes, category eyebrows, and code.
Do apply text-wrap: balance on h1–h3 elements to prevent orphan words at narrow viewports.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion — Framer Motion's useReducedMotion is already in the hero; extend to all scroll-driven animations.
Do treat each section as its own visual world. Section backgrounds, grid treatments, and motion patterns can differ.
donts: Don't use hype / hustle copy or excited-emoji energy. The brand voice is confident and specific, not motivational.
Don't use big-agency corporate aesthetics — no IBM-weight typography, no formal grid layouts.
Don't ship a generic AI-generated landing page. No hero-metric template, no cream/warm-neutral backgrounds, no floating feature icon cards, no eyebrow labels on every section heading.
Don't use warm or sand-tinted backgrounds. The entire neutral ramp is cool-tinted.
Don't add border-left colored stripes as accents on cards or callouts.
Don't use background-clip: text gradient text outside of the hero h1 .grad animation.
Don't place Geist Mono on body copy or marketing headings.
Don't use numbered section markers (01/02/03) as default scaffolding.
Don't reduce contrast for elegance — body text must read at 4.5:1 minimum against its background.
Don't ship a new card without SpringCard's cursor-glow behavior. If it's interactive, it tracks the cursor.
